source.title: Normals, subnormals and an open question

accepted.question_text: Let S be a densely defined operator on a Hilbert space with invariant domain. For each vector f in D(S), define the cyclic portion S_f by first setting D_f = {p(S)f : p belongs to C[Z]}, then H_f as the closure of D_f, and finally S_f as the restriction of S to D_f acting in the Hilbert space H_f. If every cyclic portion S_f is subnormal for every f in D(S), must the original operator S itself be subnormal?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, given a vector f ∈ D(A) set Df def ={p(A)f : p ∈ C[Z]}, Hf def = Df , Af def = A|Df . The definition of Af is in accordance with what is on p. ??nd means an operator acting in the Hilbert space Hf ; call Af the cyclic portion of A at f.
More specifically, if every Sf , for f ∈ D(S), is subnormal, is so S? (♣)
